lines.text: Maya cities in the forest, loggers on the coast and a great reef offshore. This is the story of Belize, from the Maya to independence.
Deep in the forest the Maya built Caracol, a great city that grew strong enough to defeat mighty Tikal in the year 562.
Centuries later British loggers worked the coast. In 1798 at Saint George's Caye they beat off a Spanish fleet, and the land stayed British.
George Price would lead the long road to freedom, and is remembered as the father of the nation.
Johnny Briceno would become prime minister in 2020.
Andy Palacio would carry the music of the Garifuna people to the world.
In 1961 Hurricane Hattie struck and wrecked Belize City.
So a new capital was built inland, safe from the sea. Belmopan opened in 1970.
On the twenty-first of September 1981, Belize became independent.
The colony of British Honduras was now Belize, a nation of its own on the Caribbean coast of Central America.
In 1996 its barrier reef, the longest in the Americas, was named a World Heritage Site.
From Maya temples to coral reefs, Belize guards a rich inheritance.
